sourceFinding.summary: Read all 18 owned units (s0002–s0019) in Chinese, plus each owned person's supplied items and context items. No birth or age is stated in these units. The only deaths are Hui (s0009 廆卒, AD 333 via Jinshu 108 咸和八年), Qidegui (s0010 奔死於外) and Zhao (s0014 皝殺昭), and all three are captured. The conversions are correct at year level: 建武初 is 317, 太甯末 is 325–326 and 咸和九年 is 334, with no Julian/Gregorian issue. The post-Hui sequence correctly uses a 333–334 event window rather than a chosen year. The two defects from the earlier current-source review are fixed in this candidate: claim-66 now has westernBounds onOrAfter 317, and hints-p004 is ["AD 333-334"]. All 70 items and 17 people are supported, and there are no findings. One observation outside chronology, not a finding: unitPeople lists p157 (a second 段遼 record) for s0019, but s0019 does not mention Duan Liao; 遼左 there is the region east of the Liao River. Name and mention extraction is outside this review, so it is left for the host. This is not chapter or publication approval.

sourceUnit.zh: 仁於是盡有遼左之地，自稱車騎將軍、平州刺史、遼東公。
sourceUnit.en: Ren then controlled all territory east of the Liao, proclaiming himself general of chariots and cavalry, governor of Pingzhou, and duke of Liaodong.
sourceUnit.literal: Ren thereupon wholly possessed the land left of the Liao, styled himself General of Chariots and Cavalry, governor of Ping Province, Duke of Liaodong.

retainUnits.zh: 段遼遂寇徒河，皝將張萌逆擊，敗之。
retainUnits.en: Duan Liao then invaded Tuhe, but Huang’s general Zhang Meng intercepted and routed him.
retainUnits.literal: Duan Liao thereupon raided Tuhe; Huang’s general Zhang Meng met and struck them, defeated them.

retainUnits.zh: 遼弟蘭與翰寇柳城，都尉石琮擊敗之。
retainUnits.en: Liao’s younger brother Lan together with Han raided Liucheng; commandant Shi Cong struck and defeated them.
retainUnits.literal: Liao’s younger brother Lan with Han raided Liucheng; commandant Shi Cong struck and defeated them.

retainUnits.zh: 乙連饑甚，段遼輸之粟，蘭勃要擊獲之。
retainUnits.en: When Yilian starved, Duan Liao sent grain; Lan Bo seized the convoy.
retainUnits.literal: Yilian was extremely hungry; Duan Liao sent them grain; Lan Bo intercepted and captured it.

retainUnits.zh: 遼遣將屈雲攻興國，與皝將慕容遵大戰于五官水上，雲敗，斬之，盡俘其眾。
retainUnits.en: Liao sent general Qu Yun to attack Xingguo; Yun fought a great battle with Huang’s general Murong Zun at Wuguan River, was defeated and beheaded, and his entire force was captured.
retainUnits.literal: Liao sent general Qu Yun to attack Xingguo, with Huang’s general Murong Zun fought a great battle at Wuguan River; Yun was defeated, beheaded; all captured their host.

retainUnits.zh: 及奔段遼，深為遼所敬愛。
retainUnits.en: When he fled to Duan Liao, he was deeply respected and loved by Liao.
retainUnits.literal: When he fled to Duan Liao, deeply was respected and loved by Liao.

retainUnits.zh: 後石季龍征遼，皝親將三軍略令支以北，遼議欲追之，翰知皝躬自總戎，戰必克勝，乃謂遼曰：「今石氏向至，方對大故，不宜復以小小為事。
retainUnits.en: Later when Shi Hu campaigned against Duan Liao and Murong Huang personally led an army to raid north of Lingzhi, Duan Liao debated pursuit. Knowing Huang commanded in person and must win, Murong Han told Duan Liao, "Now the Shi are about to arrive and you face a great enemy; you should not again take up small matters.
retainUnits.literal: Later Shi Jilong campaigned against Liao; Huang personally led the three armies raiding north of Lingzhi; Liao debated wishing to pursue him; Han knew Huang personally commanded the army, battle must seize victory; thereupon said to Liao: “Now the Shi clan is about to arrive, just facing great enemy; ought not again to take small matters as affairs.
